record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: Let beta be a Pisot number and let B = {0, ±1, ±2, ..., ±floor(beta)}. Is it true that Z[1/beta] ∩ [0,1) equals B[1/beta] ∩ [0,1)? Equivalently, can every element of Z[1/beta] in the unit interval be represented using powers of 1/beta with coefficients from B?

evidence.quote: To attack (W) or coincidence, it is worthy to consider a little weaker problem of algebraic nature, which is called ‘Height reducing problem’.
Problem 11. Let β be a Pisot number and put B = {0, ±1, ±2, . . . , ±bβc}. Prove Z[1/β]∩[0, 1) = B[1/β] ∩ [0, 1).

artifact.status_search_result: The general "height reducing property" — that for every algebraic number α whose conjugates all have modulus > 1 (or all = 1) there exists some finite digit set F ⊂ ℤ with ℤ[α] = F[α] — was established by Akiyama, Thuswaldner and Zaïmi (2014). However, the sharper statement with the specific minimal alphabet B = {0, ±1, …, ±⌊β⌋} for Pisot β, which is the form posed here, does not appear to have been settled and is still listed as an open problem in surveys on finiteness/periodicity of β-expansions.

status_evidence.title: Comments on the height reducing property
status_evidence.snippet: A complex number α satisfies the height reducing property if there is a finite subset F of ℤ such that ℤ[α]=F[α].
status_evidence.claim: Defines and studies the height reducing property in general.

status_evidence.title: Characterisation of the numbers which satisfy the height reducing property
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a finite F ⊂ ℤ with F[α]=ℤ[α] iff α is an algebraic number whose conjugates are all of modulus one or all of modulus greater than one.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of some finite digit set F is established, but no claim that F can be chosen as {0,±1,…,±⌊β⌋}.

status_evidence.title: Comments on the height reducing property II
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on Card(F) and an algorithm for the minimal height polynomial; the optimal/minimal alphabet question is not resolved in the Pisot case.
status_evidence.claim: The sharper version with B={0,±1,…,±⌊β⌋} remains unresolved.
